change: nativeTestResources.managedBytes 268435456 -> 536870912 (Test262 host). The copying runtime collects the whole managed graph on every cycle, so GC cost scales with the number of collections; a 256 MiB semispace halves them. Coordinator-approved memory resource limit (like the ArrayBuffer cap), not the time budget.
identity: managedBytes is a build-request field, not generated host text or AST: the historical-host baselines (test262-top-level-await, dynamic-import host, pre-service host AST) hash unchanged with no normalization; only the explicit resource pin in test262-script-service.test.ts moves. Old frozen toolchains keep their own tools and reproduce.
method: Same packages (main c9754635 == branch base 7cf9b2a6 snapshot 1a8311dd); images differ only in managedBytes. Fresh-process alternating pairs (2 per case), LLDB-contained; proc_pid_rusage V4 instructions/cycles plus sampled resident/phys-footprint maxima and ri_lifetime_max_phys_footprint (time-native-pairs-rss.ts).

memory.note: Small programs are unaffected (no-op case: 7 MiB footprint either way): the managed region is a reservation and pages become resident only as both semispaces are used. GC-heavy or long programs touch both semispaces: peak footprint ~519-568 MiB at 512 MiB vs ~262-302 MiB before.
memory.eightRunners: Worst measured case x8 runners: 4.9 GiB of inferior memory (was 2.8 GiB), against ~2-3 GB per Node runner host and 128 GB of RAM.

backlog: 1 GiB is refused today ('copying runtime allocation metadata cannot cover the managed semispace'): raising the copying runtime's allocation-metadata capacity is a separate backlog item.
